Variable Scopes374.4In Python programs, each variable has a scope in which it can be used. Variables can be categorised into local variables and global variables according to the regions they cover

Local variables38AA variable declared within a sub-program is regarded as a local variable. This variable is only valid within the sub-program.  After the sub-program has ended, all local variables will be dropped.
Global variables39BA variable declared outside a sub-program is regarded as a global variable. Its scope covers the whole program including all sub-programs.
Types of sub-programs4BSome sub-programs have neither input parameters nor return values. They usually execute default code and are mainly for printing some information in the shell.

Global variables40BTo change the value of a global variable in the sub-program, we need to use the keyword global in the sub-program to represent the global variable.Using the keyword global to refer to the global variable score

Parameters Passing434.5When calling a sub-program that requires an input parameter, the actual parameter will be passed to the formal parameter.

Passing immutable objects44AIn Python, integers (int), floats (float), Booleans (bool) and strings (str) are immutable objects. When calling a sub-program and passing an immutable object, the value of the actual parameter will be copied to the formal parameter of the sub-program.
Passing immutable objects45AModifications made to the formal parameter within the sub-program do not affect the value in the actual parameter.

Passing mutable objects46BLists (list) are mutable objects in Python. When calling a sub-program and passing a mutable object, the formal parameter of the sub-program will store the computer memory address of the actual parameter. The formal parameter is the pointer of the actual parameter. When the sub-program is being run, the formal parameter will refer to the memory address of the actual parameter.
Passing mutable objects47BTherefore, any modifications made to the formal parameter within the sub-program will be reflected in the actual parameter.

Stubs534.6Due to the benefits of modularisation, we often break down a complex program into multiple sub-programs.

Stubs544.6When our main program has many sub-programs, we may encounter the following two problems:When we have not finished writing all the sub-programs, the whole program cannot function properly, or even cannot be compiled.When an error occurs in the program, it is hard for us to determine which sub-program causes the problem.

Stubs554.6Therefore, we need to use stubs. They replace the main body of sub-programs by short, simple and temporary code, allowing the main program to run even when the sub-programs have not been completed.Stubs without a return value:Stubs with a return value:

Types of sub-programs6BThis type of sub-programs have return values even though there are no input parameters. They can produce return values without relying on parameters. Some of these sub-programs directly use variables in the program to perform operations instead of obtaining input values in the form of parameters.
Types of sub-programs7BThis type of sub-programs have input parameters and return values.
